event: Americans with Disabilities Act signed into law
applies_to: Employers, state and local governments (Title II), places of public accommodation (Title III)
summary: The ADA prohibits disability discrimination. Title II covers state and local governments. Title III covers private businesses open to the public. The statute does not mention websites.
source_title: ADA.gov: Americans with Disabilities Act

event: Section 508 amended to require accessible federal electronic and information technology
applies_to: Federal agencies and their ICT procurement
summary: The Rehabilitation Act Amendments of 1998 strengthened Section 508, creating the procurement-driven requirements federal contractors and vendors still answer to through VPATs.
source_title: Section508.gov: Laws and Policies

event: WCAG 2.0 becomes a W3C Recommendation
applies_to: Web content
summary: WCAG 2.0 introduces the four principles and the A, AA, AAA conformance levels. It later became the technical basis for the Section 508 refresh and for early web accessibility settlements.
source_title: W3C: WCAG 2.0

event: Section 508 Refresh final rule published
applies_to: Federal agencies and ICT procurement
summary: The Access Board updated its ICT standards to incorporate WCAG 2.0 A and AA by reference. Federal agencies had to comply starting January 18, 2018.
source_title: U.S. Access Board: ICT Standards and Guidelines

event: DOJ withdraws its Title III web accessibility rulemaking
applies_to: Private businesses (Title III)
summary: DOJ published a notice withdrawing four previously announced ADA rulemakings, including the advance notice on website accessibility for Title III entities. Since then, there has been no federal technical regulation for private-sector websites, so courts and settlements set the working standard.
source_title: Federal Register: Notice of Withdrawal of Four Previously Announced Rulemaking Actions

event: WCAG 2.1 becomes a W3C Recommendation
applies_to: Web content
summary: WCAG 2.1 adds 17 success criteria focused on mobile, low vision, and cognitive accessibility. It is the standard named in the DOJ Title II rule and the HHS Section 504 rule.
source_title: W3C: WCAG 2.1

event: Ninth Circuit holds ADA applies to Domino's website and app (Robles v. Domino's Pizza)
authority: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
applies_to: Private businesses with a physical nexus to websites and apps
summary: The Ninth Circuit held that the ADA applies to a business website and app that connect customers to goods and services of a physical place of public accommodation. It also said due process did not bar the claim even though DOJ had issued no web regulation.
source_title: Ninth Circuit opinion, No. 17-55504

event: Ontario AODA deadline for large organizations to meet WCAG 2.0 AA on public websites
applies_to: Designated public sector organizations and large private and non-profit organizations (50+ employees)
summary: Under the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, covered organizations had to make public websites and web content published after January 1, 2012 conform to WCAG 2.0 AA by January 1, 2021, with exceptions for live captions and pre-recorded audio description.
source_title: Ontario.ca: How to make websites accessible

event: DOJ issues guidance on web accessibility and the ADA
applies_to: State and local governments (Title II) and businesses (Title III)
technical_standard: WCAG referenced as one way to comply
summary: DOJ restated its longstanding position that the ADA applies to web content and described practical steps. The guidance is not a regulation and does not name a mandatory standard for Title III.
source_title: ADA.gov: Guidance on Web Accessibility and the ADA

event: WCAG 2.2 becomes a W3C Recommendation
applies_to: Web content
summary: WCAG 2.2 adds nine success criteria (including Target Size Minimum, Dragging Movements, Focus Not Obscured, and Accessible Authentication) and removes 4.1.1 Parsing. It is backward compatible with WCAG 2.1.
source_title: W3C: WCAG 2.2

event: DOJ publishes the Title II web and mobile app accessibility final rule
applies_to: State and local government entities (Title II)
summary: The final rule (28 CFR Part 35) requires web content and mobile apps of state and local governments to conform to WCAG 2.1 AA. Original compliance dates were April 24, 2026 (population 50,000 or more) and April 26, 2027 (smaller entities and special districts).
source_title: Federal Register: Accessibility of Web Information and Services of State and Local Government Entities

event: HHS publishes the Section 504 web, mobile app, and kiosk accessibility final rule
authority: Department of Health and Human Services
applies_to: Recipients of HHS federal financial assistance
summary: The rule requires recipients of HHS financial assistance to make web content and mobile apps conform to WCAG 2.1 AA. Original compliance dates were May 11, 2026 (15 or more employees) and May 10, 2027 (fewer than 15 employees).
source_title: Federal Register: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance

event: European Accessibility Act requirements start to apply
applies_to: Covered consumer products and services, including e-commerce, banking services, and e-books
technical_standard: EN 301 549 (which incorporates WCAG 2.1 AA for web content)
summary: Directive (EU) 2019/882 sets accessibility requirements for a defined list of products and services offered to EU consumers. Member states apply national laws from June 28, 2025. Microenterprises providing services have a limited exemption.
source_title: EUR-Lex: Directive (EU) 2019/882

event: DOJ extends Title II web rule compliance dates by one year (Interim Final Rule)
applies_to: State and local government entities (Title II)
summary: The Interim Final Rule (91 FR 20902) moves the compliance date for entities with a population of 50,000 or more from April 24, 2026 to April 26, 2027, and for smaller entities and special district governments from April 26, 2027 to April 26, 2028. The WCAG 2.1 AA standard and the scope of the rule are unchanged.
source_title: Federal Register: Extension of Compliance Dates (DOJ Title II)

event: Original DOJ Title II compliance date for entities serving 50,000 or more people (superseded)
applies_to: State and local government entities with a population of 50,000 or more
summary: Superseded by the April 20, 2026 Interim Final Rule. Still cited incorrectly in many guides and vendor pages.
source_title: Federal Register: Extension of Compliance Dates (DOJ Title II)

event: HHS extends Section 504 web rule compliance dates by one year (Interim Final Rule)
authority: Department of Health and Human Services
applies_to: Recipients of HHS federal financial assistance
summary: The Interim Final Rule (91 FR 25496) moves the compliance date for recipients with 15 or more employees from May 11, 2026 to May 11, 2027, and for recipients with fewer than 15 employees from May 10, 2027 to May 10, 2028.
source_title: Federal Register: Extension of Compliance Dates (HHS Section 504)

event: Original HHS Section 504 compliance date for recipients with 15 or more employees (superseded)
authority: Department of Health and Human Services
applies_to: Recipients of HHS financial assistance with 15 or more employees
summary: Superseded by the May 11, 2026 Interim Final Rule.
source_title: Federal Register: Extension of Compliance Dates (HHS Section 504)

event: DOJ Title II compliance date: state and local governments with population of 50,000 or more
applies_to: State and local government entities with a population of 50,000 or more
summary: Web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, subject to the exceptions listed in the rule.
source_title: Federal Register: Extension of Compliance Dates (DOJ Title II)

event: HHS Section 504 compliance date: recipients with 15 or more employees
authority: Department of Health and Human Services
applies_to: Recipients of HHS financial assistance with 15 or more employees
summary: Web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA.
source_title: Federal Register: Extension of Compliance Dates (HHS Section 504)

event: DOJ Title II compliance date: population under 50,000 and special district governments
applies_to: Public entities with a population under 50,000 and special district governments
summary: Web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA, subject to the exceptions listed in the rule.
source_title: Federal Register: Extension of Compliance Dates (DOJ Title II)

event: HHS Section 504 compliance date: recipients with fewer than 15 employees
authority: Department of Health and Human Services
applies_to: Recipients of HHS financial assistance with fewer than 15 employees
summary: Web content and mobile apps must conform to WCAG 2.1 AA.
source_title: Federal Register: Extension of Compliance Dates (HHS Section 504)
